questions.q: What are the two parts of self-awareness?
a: Knowing yourself and knowing how others see you
Knowing your feelings and controlling them
Knowing your values and pursuing your goals
Knowing your strengths and hiding your weaknesses
questions.why: Lesson 1 separates internal self-awareness from external self-awareness.

questions.q: Which seven areas does Eurich say you must understand to be fully self-aware?
a: Values, passions, aspirations, fit, patterns, reactions and impact
Habits, goals, finances, health, family, work and rest
Strengths, weaknesses, fears, hopes, skills, roles and image
Beliefs, emotions, routines, relationships, purpose, focus and growth
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the seven insights, from values and passions to reactions and impact on others.

questions.q: Why can too much self-analysis backfire?
a: We accept easy explanations without questioning them
It takes time away from work and relationships
It makes us too dependent on other people
It forces us to relive painful memories
questions.why: Lesson 2 says self-analyzers end up more anxious and rarely check whether their conclusions are true.

questions.q: What question does Eurich recommend asking instead of why?
a: What do I think, feel and do in this situation?
Who is to blame for how I ended up here?
When will I finally change this pattern?
Why do I keep making the same mistake?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says asking what, or who, helps you name emotions and cope with them.

questions.q: What is the first step in using feedback well?
a: Make sure you understand what the person means
Decide immediately whether you agree
Ask several people for the same criticism
Wait a day before responding to it
questions.why: Lesson 3 says receiving feedback starts with accurate understanding, asking for clarification if needed.
